items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Public APIs have docstrings. But the `syncCommit` and `durabilityManager` fields have no comments, and the long durability predicate `(seqNum == 0 && (totalDurableCommits > 0 || highestDurableSeqNum > 0)) || ...` is copied 3+ times inline instead of being named.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: durability.go is 544 lines, which exceeds the 500-line cap. WaitForDurabilityContext and WaitForJobDurabilityContext are long and repeat the same check logic. The DB fields (durabilityQueue, durabilityLoopDone) and the wrapping of syncWG inside commitWrite spread the tracking across db.go.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Close and context handling are done carefully. However, `d.durabilityQueue <- sc` is sent inside commitWrite while commit.mu is held, so it can block. Retention and subscription limits default to the magic numbers 1024 and 4096. Correctness depends on applyDone being closed exactly once.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: The API changes are additive. But every sync commit now allocates a `syncCommit` plus a channel and goes through a background goroutine before `origWG.Done()`, even when BatchDurable is unset. Sync=true commits made with NoSyncWait are also wrapped and tracked, which changes their fsync path.
